doc.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996

title: Van Morrison compared to Duke Ellington
summary: He tells Van Morrison he reminds him of Duke Ellington in picking musicians for what they do on the tune.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Oh, my. Well this has really been fascinating. You tired yet, because we can keep talking if you want.
We are so glad you were able to join us, and I want to wish you the best of luck with Van Morrison. I hope he’s up to playing next to you.

Are you kidding? He’s always — you know I’ll tell you something about him. We were riding in a car in Chicago, and I said, “Listen, I’m not kissing your behind, but I want to tell you something, you remind me of Duke Ellington.” He said, “In what way?” I says, “If you need a musician, a horn, saxophone, whatever, for two bars, that’s all you want them for.” He said, “You’re right.” I said, “That’s the way Duke was.” Whether you could read or not didn’t make a difference. If you could do what he wanted on that tune, that’s all he was interested in. And Morrison is the same way. Van Morrison.
They know how to pick the right people.
They know how to pick, yeah. They take their music serious.
I do. It’s a personal thing with me.
